# Google Antigravity: A New Era in AI-Assisted Software Development or Just Another Fork?

In the ever-evolving landscape of software development, Google has introduced a new tool named Antigravity, sparking a flurry of discussions among tech enthusiasts and developers alike. Positioned as a potential game-changer in AI-assisted coding, Antigravity is being perceived with a mix of intrigue and skepticism.

## A Familiar Framework

Upon closer examination, many users have noted that Antigravity appears to be a fork of Visual Studio Code (VSCode), a popular code editor used by countless developers worldwide. One user voiced their disappointment, stating, “It’s actually disrespectful of Google to launch this without even a mention of the fact that it is based on VSCode.” This sentiment resonates with several others who feel that the lack of acknowledgment for the foundational work of VSCode undermines the credibility of Google’s latest offering.

## The AI Models Behind Antigravity

Antigravity supports a variety of AI models, including Google’s own Gemini and other notable options like Claude Sonnet and GPT-OSS. This integration suggests that Google is leveraging its Cloud capabilities rather than relying on external services to power the AI functionalities of Antigravity. One user pointed out, “Interesting that they include non-Gemini models... I assume that Antigravity is using GC as the provider.”

## User Experience: A Mixed Bag

While the promise of AI-assisted coding is enticing, users have encountered several frustrations. Reports of issues with the account setup process have surfaced, with many users getting stuck on the "Setting Up Your Account" page. This has led to speculation about the stability of the platform, especially for those using workspace accounts. "My guess is it fails if you use a workspace account," one commenter noted, highlighting the confusion surrounding account compatibility.

Additionally, the website's user interface has been criticized for its scrolling functionality, which some users found disorienting. A frustrated commenter remarked, “Google likes to mess with basic browser functionality... Seems like a lot of work to do just to make something shittier.”

## The Broader Implications

As with any new technology, there are concerns regarding privacy and data usage. One user raised a question that many developers are likely pondering: “If I use this, does it mean Google has access to all my code?” While assurances regarding data privacy have been mentioned, the ambiguity surrounding terms of service often leaves users wary of how their information may be used.

## Conclusion: A Fork in the Road

As Google unveils Antigravity, the tech community is left to grapple with its implications. Is this the dawn of a new era in AI-assisted software development, or merely another fork in the long line of coding tools? While the potential is there, the execution and transparency surrounding its development will ultimately determine its place in the software development ecosystem.
